slot.brief: Unpolarized light reflected off a glass surface; use Brewster's law to identify the angle at which reflected light becomes polarized, given refractive index.

stem: Unpolarized light travels inside glass of refractive index $\sqrt{3}$ and is incident on a glass–air surface. At what angle of incidence to the normal is the reflected light completely plane-polarized?

verdicts.working: For glass to air, θ_B = arctan(n_air/n_glass) = arctan(1/√3) = 30°.

working:
$\tan i_B=\dfrac{n_{\text{air}}}{n_{\text{glass}}}=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$; hence $i_B=30^\circ$.

Independent check: For glass to air, θ_B = arctan(n_air/n_glass) = arctan(1/√3) = 30°.
